messages:
olivia_csm: Quick pulse for this week's account health check — noticed a 3.2% → 7.8% jump in overall error rate for Top10 accounts since Tue morning. Adding quick breakdown and asking infra/SRE for triage. chart: https://dash.redwood.ai/health/1783

maria_cs: Which error class is driving this? 5xx vs timeouts vs rate-limits? Any particular customer impacted more?

olivia_csm: Mostly 5xx and timeouts. Rate limits up for one high-volume tenant (acme-inc) due to a recent campaign. Attached quick table from console: 
- 5xx: 54% of errors (spike at 03:20 UTC Tue)
- timeouts ( downstream ): 30% (p90 latency for inference route spiked to 12s)
- rate_limit: 16% (client-side bursts)

olivia_csm: Top failing endpoints by error count last 48h: 
1) POST /v1/generate (model: gptx-8k) — 42% of 5xx
2) POST /v1/embeddings — 18% timeouts + 5xx mix
3) POST /v1/streaming (sdk) — 12% rate_limit + partial 5xx
4) POST /v1/parse (custom tooling) — 9% 5xx

dan_sre: Thanks. I'll pull logs. Can you paste an example auth/key and request id from a failing trace? Need request ids to follow KV cache/slot errors.

olivia_csm: Example from yesterday 2026-03-19 03:21:14 UTC — request_id: r_8f3a2c91, client: acme-inc, route: /v1/generate, status: 502, error: "upstream inference runtime error: kernel OOM on layer 14"

lee_infra: Kernel OOM on layer 14 suggests we hit a quantized kernel path with an unexpected sequence length. I'm going to check node gpu utilization and model variant routing. Running quick grep in runtime logs: 
```
[2026-03-19T03:21:14Z] r_8f3a2c91 model=gptx-8k node=gpu-14 kernel=kv_cache_exec layer=14 alloc_fail
[2026-03-19T03:21:14Z] r_8f3a2c91 fallback=soft-fail routed_to=gptx-8k-quant
```

ben_eng: Also seeing timeouts where worker retries exceed 3 and client resets. Example trace: r_9b4d1e22 route=/v1/embeddings latency=11.8s retries=4 status=504. Likely caused by long-running cold starts on large-context workloads.

maria_cs: For acme-inc, they had a marketing send at Tue 02:30 UTC generating lots of long prompts (avg prompt length 2.8k tokens). I flagged renewals last quarter — this could increase churn risk if we don't stabilize.

olivia_csm: Renewal risk: medium for acme-inc if errors continue >5% of their calls. Action items: triage infra, set temporary client throttling, enable fallback smaller model for generate.

dan_sre: Triage plan: 
- (IN-PROG) Inspect node gpu-14 mem + eviction logs (lee)
- (IN-PROG) Check model variant routing rules for gptx-8k quant fallback (ben)
- (TODO) Add temporary per-client soft-throttle for acme-inc burst windows via routing policy (maria + ops)
- (TODO) Add quick alert rule: if 5xx rate > 5% for any account for 30m, page oncall

lee_infra: Found correlated kernel OOMs on 3 nodes (gpu-10/14/23). There's an autoscale lag in the pool causing denser packing. Patch incoming to reduce packing threshold from 0.85 -> 0.7. Deploying now. deploy_bot: deployment started: autoscaler/packing-adjust v1.2.3

ben_eng: I'm pushing a conservative fallback mapping: route /v1/generate for gptx-8k -> gptx-4k-small when sequence > 3k tokens or GPU load > 70%. Will roll canary to 10% traffic first.

maria_cs: I'll reach out to acme-inc CSM and share mitigation plan + temp throttle. Also prepping a usage report to show cost impact and recommended prompt engineering tips.

olivia_csm: Great. Can SRE confirm if timeouts on embeddings are same root cause or separate (network vs runtime)?

dan_sre: embeddings timeouts look like a mix: some network egress hiccups to third-party vector store (10% of timeout traces include outbound connect errors), rest are cold-start runtime. I'll open two tickets: INF-4782 (runtime cold-start) and NET-992 (egress retry/backoff).

maria_cs: Anything I should tell the customer now? Suggested script: "We're seeing transient errors on high-volume long prompts; we've deployed autoscaler/packing adjustments and a conservative fallback to reduce failures. We'll throttle surges short-term and follow up with detailed RCA."

olivia_csm: Perfect. Assign owners and timelines in the ticket. I'll update weekly health deck Friday with pre/post metrics. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
